title: look closer
summary: An endless zoom through five paintings, each one in the middle of the last: a room at night, an autumn street, a bakery, a frozen lake, a reef, and the room again. Painted in code with short brush strokes.

specs.paintings: 5, each 2048 × 2048, painted when the page loads
specs.the trick: every painting has a transparent square in the middle, a third of its width, framed by something in the scene; the next painting is drawn behind it at a third of the size
specs.the chain: a framed painting on a wall → a bakery window → a postcard → a hole in the ice → a gilded frame sunk in the sand → the first room
specs.brush: about 90,000 short strokes per painting, each taking its colour from the shapes underneath and its direction from a flow field
specs.controls: scroll, drag or the arrow keys to walk in or back out; space pauses; left alone it drifts inward
specs.inspired by: the infinite zoom website by @kevin_t_ngo, posted on X (the format only: his paintings were generated images; these five are drawn in code)
